literal: abundantly having done, oneself those who despise, to smile having made, within friendship to die embracing is the nature.
translation: When dealing with those who show exaggerated affection but secretly despise you, it is wise to make them smile outwardly while letting the friendship die in your embrace.
modern: வெளியில் மிகவும் அன்பாக நடந்துகொண்டு உள்ளத்தில் தம்மை இகழ்பவர்களை, வெளியிலும் சிரித்து மகிழும்படி செய்து, ஆனால் அகத்தில் அந்த நட்பு சாகும்படி பழகுவதே அறிவுடையோர் இயல்பாகும்.
explanation: This couplet advises on how to handle false friends who show exaggerated affection outwardly but mock you inwardly. Instead of confronting them, one should match their outward behavior by making them smile and acting friendly. However, internally, one should let the friendship wither and die, maintaining only a superficial embrace. The word 'சா' (to die) powerfully contrasts with 'புல்லல்' (embracing), showing that the relationship should be allowed to perish even while maintaining outward pleasantries.
